Why these elements are here
  • Patient rail. Keeps the current queue visible while staff inspect one person. Each row shows a patient and a meaningful state.
  • Clinical record first. Makes the existing recommendation the starting point, rather than an AI conversation or a generated summary.
  • Latest exchange only. Shows what changed without making staff read every message. Full conversation history can sit one level deeper in the implemented product.
  • Explicit next step. Answers who is expected to act next and what the coordinator will do afterward.
  • Shared source and connection sections. Gives the same visibility as the register while dedicating more space to patient context. Best for frequent case inspection.
Static design study. Fictional records and connection states; no live systems.
